description:
## Intent

The second half of v0.4 (plan phase row: *"Rich popover …, settings, health/stale UI, update line"*): give the menubar a settings surface, make health and staleness visible and honest, and add the passive update notice. This ticket turns three plan commitments into UI: (1) the phase-gated title-mode picker, (2) "quiet self-heal + health dot + doctor" (Quality bar rulings) with stale-but-honest freshness, (3) "Passive update line; never self-mutating updates" (Onboarding section).

## Scope

**In:**
- **Settings surface**: launch-at-login toggle, refresh interval, title-mode picker. The picker exposes ONLY shipped modes — $ today + burn $/hr in this phase; quota joins in v0.5 via T-022 (plan, UI: *"mode picker exposes only shipped modes ($ + burn v0.3; quota v0.5)"*).
- **Health dot**: reflects service/helper health — service reachable over the control socket, helper crash-loop breaker state (T-014 sets health on N exits/60 s).
- **Stale greying**: menubar title greys when the rendered dataset's generatedAt/provenance is stale. Must be driven by **per-dataset provenance** — the snapshot schema deliberately has *"no global stale flag"*; freshness is derived per requested range/fields (plan, Snapshot schema). Failure stays bounded to stale-but-honest, never wrong-and-confident.
- **Update line**: a passive "new version available" line in the dropdown/popover. **Never self-mutating updates** — no auto-update, no touching the install; the launcher/registry healing model (plan, Launcher section) assumes upgrades happen through the package manager plus explicit repair. The check itself is **background, cached, bounded, and fail-silent** (ISS-045): it runs off the rendering path and the UI only ever reads a cached result — rendering never awaits the network; the request carries a validated finite deadline that, on expiry, **aborts and disposes the underlying request** rather than merely ceasing to wait for it (racing a timer does not cancel the operation — the bounded-wait rule T-008's findings had to re-learn twice); and every failure shape — immediate connection error, DNS failure, or a blackholed connection that is accepted and never answered — degrades to "no line shown", never an error and never a hang.

**Out:** SMAppService login item (needs flat .app — T-021); notifications (T-021); the popover layout itself (T-019); quota mode and floating-widget toggle (T-022).

## Approach notes

- Launch-at-login sits on top of T-015's LaunchAgent + launcher machinery (plist targets the launcher; menubar agent is Aqua-limited). The toggle must go through the same installation-ID-owned registry path — it must not become a second, competing mechanism that fights `service install/start/stop` desired-state persistence. In v0.5 the flat .app may migrate this to SMAppService (T-021).
- Onboarding already prompts for "service + login item" consent; this settings toggle is the post-install home of that same choice — keep them consistent.
- `doctor` (v0.3) already detects and explains launcher/plist/freshness problems; the health dot is the glanceable summary of the same signals, not a new diagnostic system. Monotonicity violations are an anomaly *signal* only.
- The update-check deadline value is **validated where the mistake would land**, not passed raw to a timer: 0, negative, NaN and Infinity are refused at configuration (T-008 findings §4.1 — unvalidated injectable deadlines silently clamp to fire immediately or wait forever).

## Constraints

- Update check must be passive, non-mutating, background, cached, and bounded; zero lifecycle scripts remains a hard property of the package.
- `usage.py` frozen oracle untouched; `package.json` carries no author field; no real transcript data or personal paths in fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Settings surface exposes exactly three controls: launch-at-login toggle, refresh interval, and a title-mode picker listing only $-today and burn modes (no quota entry present in v0.4)
2. Launch-at-login toggle enables/disables login-item behavior through the existing launcher/LaunchAgent path (installation-ID-owned registry) and round-trips correctly across a menubar quit + relaunch; it does not conflict with `service install/start/stop` desired-state
3. Health dot visibly changes state when (a) the service is unreachable over the control socket and (b) the helper crash-loop breaker has tripped; returns to healthy after recovery
4. Menubar title greys when the rendered dataset's provenance/generatedAt exceeds the staleness threshold, driven by per-dataset provenance (demonstrably not a single global stale flag), and un-greys after a successful refresh
5. When a newer published version exists, a passive "new version available" line appears in the dropdown; selecting or ignoring it never modifies the installation, spawns installers, or writes outside spendbar's own state dirs. The check runs off the rendering path and the UI reads only its cached result; on every failure — including no network at all — the line is simply absent and no error is surfaced
6. Refresh-interval changes take effect in the service's full-tier scheduling without violating the at-most-one-attempt-per-interval cap
7. Bounded-wait proof for the update check (ISS-045): against a test server that accepts the connection and never responds, the menubar remains responsive throughout (title updates and menu interaction unaffected), the validated finite deadline fires, and when it fires the underlying request is aborted and its resources disposed — asserted directly (no leaked socket/handle after the deadline), not inferred from the UI. Deadline validation refuses 0, negative, NaN and Infinity

## Risks
Two mechanisms fighting: a launch-at-login toggle that bypasses the launcher registry would recreate the exact silent-retarget/ownership hazards the round-2/3 launcher redesign eliminated. Staleness UI is a trust surface — a global stale flag or optimistic freshness would violate the stale-but-honest ruling that anchors the product's accuracy positioning. Update checking adds the project's first network call from the UI surface; unbounded it hangs the menubar behind exactly the common failure shapes (captive portal, dropped VPN — a connection accepted and never answered), which is why ISS-045 requires background isolation, caching, a resource-disposing deadline, and fail-silent degradation; it must also stay passive or it breaks the zero-self-mutation promise.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Where do settings persist — extend the existing config file (usage-config.json lineage) or a new per-user state file — and what schema/versioning? Plan is silent.
2. Refresh-interval bounds and default value (plan gives the scheduling cap semantics but no numbers).
3. Staleness threshold(s) for greying — fixed, derived from refresh interval, or per-dataset? Plan defines the provenance mechanism but not the UI threshold.
4. Update-check mechanism and cadence (npm registry query? which endpoint? how often? cached where?) — plan mandates only 'passive line; never self-mutating'. Whatever is chosen must satisfy the background/cached/bounded/fail-silent contract above; the open question is the mechanism, not the contract.
5. Is the settings surface native SwiftUI in the helper, or CLI-backed (`spendbar setup`-style) with the helper as a thin trigger? Depends partly on T-019's spike outcome.
title: Settings, health/stale UI, update-notifier line
